balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For The Estée Lauder Companies Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

categoryRevenue.title: Net sales by product category
categoryRevenue.content:
Estée Lauder discloses net sales across five product categories: Skin Care, Makeup, Fragrance, Hair Care and a small Other residual.

For The Estée Lauder Companies Inc.: Skin Care is historically the largest and most profitable category but is also the most exposed to Asia travel-retail and China destocking -- it fell every year from FY2023 through FY2025 as that channel worked through excess inventory. Fragrance has been the standout grower over the same stretch, driven by prestige fragrance launches and less exposed to the China/travel-retail channel. The FY2023-FY2025 group decline the PRGP restructuring was launched to address shows up first and hardest in this chart, not in the blended Revenue line.

What to watch:

  • Whether Skin Care has stabilized or is still shrinking as a share of the mix
  • Fragrance and Hair Care's share of growth versus the larger, slower categories
  • Interim rows show the category seasonality (fragrance gifting skews to H1/holiday quarters)

regionRevenue.title: Net sales by region (current structure)
regionRevenue.content:
Net sales by region under the current structure EL adopted in FY2024: Americas, Europe/Middle East/Africa plus travel retail ("EUKEM"), Asia/Pacific, and a separately broken-out Mainland China. Before FY2024 the company reported a different Americas/EMEA/APAC split with travel retail and Mainland China folded into APAC -- those legacy figures are not shown here because they are not comparable to the current-structure series.

For The Estée Lauder Companies Inc.: Mainland China and Asia travel retail were the epicenter of the FY2023-FY2025 inventory destocking and demand slowdown that triggered the PRGP restructuring, so splitting China out from the rest of Asia/Pacific is the single most informative cut of this company's regional story right now.

What to watch:

  • Mainland China's trajectory versus the rest of Asia/Pacific
  • Whether Americas and EMEA growth is offsetting Asia weakness
  • Only FY2024 onward is populated under this structure -- do not compare levels to pre-FY2024 regional figures from other charts or filings

constantCurrency.title: Constant-currency revenue growth
constantCurrency.content:
Constant-currency revenue growth restates prior-period results at current-period exchange rates, stripping out the effect of currency translation so the growth rate reflects volume and price alone.

For The Estée Lauder Companies Inc.: this is management's preferred headline growth metric on earnings calls, and the gap between it and reported (as-reported currency) revenue growth matters for EL specifically because a majority of net sales are earned outside the US -- a strong dollar can make reported growth look worse (or a weak dollar make it look better) than the underlying business performance.

What to watch:

  • Gap between this chart and the reported YoY % in the Revenue chart above -- a wide gap means FX, not the business, is driving the headline number
  • Whether the sign flips (FY2026 moved positive after three negative constant-currency years)

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For The Estée Lauder Companies Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For The Estée Lauder Companies Inc.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For The Estée Lauder Companies Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For The Estée Lauder Companies Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For The Estée Lauder Companies Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For The Estée Lauder Companies Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For The Estée Lauder Companies Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For The Estée Lauder Companies Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For The Estée Lauder Companies Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
